originalTitle: Sony isn’t phasing out discs quite as quickly as we thought

content: Sony isn’t backing away from its decision to kill the video game disc in January 2028. But Sony isn’t shutting down production as quickly as we thought, either. Two months after reports that Sony’s last discmaking plant was already being repurposed, the company’s discmaking division now says that one widely reported detail was wrong. Originally, it sounded like the division’s president said the Thalgau plant would produce 90 percent fewer discs in 2028 — but the reality is it will only produce 10 percent fewer discs in 2028, an unnamed Sony DADC spokesperson told Game journalist Brian Crecente. “To clarify and avoid any misleading information: in that statement Dietmar anticipated an overall product volume decline by 10 percent, not a decline down to 10 percent,” the spokesperson said. Sony DADC did not respond to The Verge’s fact-check request, including our question about whether the division is still restructuring and retraining every single one of the plant’s 300 employees to work on microlenses instead of discs, as ORF Austria reported in July. It wouldn’t tell Crecente any more details, either. One reason that the discmaking plant might take longer to transition: Even if Sony won’t produce brand-new games on disc after the January 2028 cutoff, the company will continue to let publishers “place re-orders for existing PlayStation disc games.” Even if PlayStation discs stick around longer than we thought, the future isn’t looking good for the concept of video game ownership. Several major game publishers are conspicuously missing from Microsoft’s disc-to-digital initiative, and Sony keeps giving gamers reason to believe it doesn’t respect the idea of ownership at all. Most recently, Sony made the breathtakingly blunt legal argument that “reasonable consumers” couldn’t possibly believe they own a game after they buy it — because if they truly owned a game, how could multiple copies exist at a time?
chineseTitle: 索尼并没有像我们想象的那么快地淘汰光盘
chineseSummary: 索尼并没有放弃在 2028 年 1 月取消视频游戏光盘的决定。但索尼也没有像我们想象的那么快停止生产。两个月后，有报道称索尼最后一家光盘制造厂已被重新利用，该公司的光盘制造部门现在表示，一项广泛报道的细节是错误的。起初， […]
chineseContent: 索尼并没有放弃在 2028 年 1 月取消视频游戏光盘的决定。但索尼也没有像我们想象的那么快停止生产。两个月后，有报道称索尼最后一家光盘制造工厂已被重新利用，该公司的光盘制造部门现在表示，一项广泛报道的细节是错误的。一位不愿透露姓名的索尼 DADC 发言人告诉 Game 记者 Brian Crecente，最初，听起来该部门总裁表示 Thalgau 工厂到 2028 年的光盘产量将减少 90%，但实际情况是到 2028 年该工厂的光盘产量只会减少 10%。 “为了澄清并避免任何误导性信息：在该声明中，Dietmar 预计整体产品销量将下降 10%，而不是下降至 10%，”该发言人表示。正如 ORF Austria 在 7 月报道的那样，索尼 DADC 没有回应 The Verge 的事实核查请求，包括我们询问该部门是否仍在重组和再培训该工厂 300 名员工中的每一位，以从事微透镜而非光盘工作。它也不会告诉克雷森特更多细节。光盘制造厂可能需要更长时间过渡的原因之一是：即使索尼在 2028 年 1 月停产后不再生产全新的光盘游戏，该公司仍将继续让发行商“重新订购现有的 PlayStation 光盘游戏”。即使 PlayStation 光盘的存在时间比我们想象的要长，但视频游戏所有权概念的未来看起来并不美好。几家主要的游戏发行商显然没有参与微软的光盘到数字计划，而索尼不断让游戏玩家有理由相信它根本不尊重所有权的想法。最近，索尼提出了令人震惊的直言不讳的法律论点，即“理性的消费者”不能”
